domain_restrictions: n is a positive integer (so n is nonzero)
j is an integer satisfying 0 <= j <= n - 1
x is a real number satisfying j/n <= x and x < (j + 1)/n
J_{n,j}(d) is evaluated as j/n + d for the given n, j, and real d
semantic_sketch_json.normalized_claim: Given n in positive integers, j in integers with 0 <= j <= n - 1, and x in reals with j/n <= x < (j + 1)/n, let d be defined by d = x - j/n. Then d satisfies 0 <= d < 1/n, and x equals J_{n,j}(d) where J_{n,j}(d) = j/n + d.
quantifier_order: for all integers j with 0 <= j <= n - 1
for all real numbers x with j/n <= x < (j + 1)/n
define d as x minus j/n

statement_nl: Let n be a positive integer and j an integer with 0 <= j <= n - 1. If x is a real number with j/n <= x < (j + 1)/n and d = x - j/n, then 0 <= d < 1/n and x = J_{n,j}(d), where J_{n,j}(d) = j/n + d.
